themes.label: Account lockout and identity verification failures
themes.summary: Users are locked out of their accounts after logging in or changing a password, then cannot pass identity verification through Persona (ID photo, selfie, or phone/email code), often looping back to the verification screen or hitting attempt limits. Many report no working path to human support because the help flow itself requires logging in, and some say new accounts get restricted within days. Problems appear on both Android and iOS across several recent app versions, and the complaints are concentrated in recent months.
themes.recommendation: Audit the Persona verification integration end to end, starting with logs of rejected ID and selfie checks grouped by platform, app version, and ID country, and add a logged-out support path (such as a web form tied to the verification session) so locked-out users can reach a human reviewer.

themes.label: Locked accounts stuck in verification loop
themes.summary: Users report their LinkedIn accounts were restricted, often for suspected security issues or with no stated reason, and that identity verification through Persona or document upload repeatedly fails or loops back on itself. Many say support is automated, unreachable while locked out (since contacting support requires signing in), and slow to respond, with some users losing access for months. Reports span Android and iOS across several recent app versions, and several mention failed sign-in with a generic "Something unexpected happened" error.
themes.recommendation: Audit the Persona identity verification and restriction-appeal pipeline for false rejections and loops by logging verification outcomes per device and app version, and add a logged-out support path that does not require signing in to submit an appeal.

themes.label: Post-update crashes and forced logouts
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android report that after recent app updates the app crashes on launch or while scrolling the feed, logs them out repeatedly, or gets stuck during posting and image uploads. Many say reinstalling, clearing cache, and updating did not help, and several note the problems began right after a specific version (such as v9.1.411 or v4.1.1215). A subset also says older phones or older iOS versions are now blocked from using the app, with prompts to update that they cannot satisfy.
themes.recommendation: Pull crash and session logs segmented by app version (iOS 9.1.410 to 9.1.533, Android 4.1.1215 to 4.1.1238) and OS version, and identify the regression that causes launch crashes, forced re-login, and stuck image uploads. Also confirm the minimum supported iOS and Android OS versions and make the update prompt state the exact requirement with a working fallback.

themes.label: Forced updates break older devices
themes.summary: This cluster mixes many complaints, but a recurring thread is users being pushed to update the app and then hitting problems: iPhone 6S and iPhone 13 owners say they cannot install the required version, and some say the latest update logs them out or leaves them unable to log in. Other reviews cover slow or overheating performance, verification problems, unwanted premium prompts, and notification overload, so the theme is broad rather than tightly focused.
themes.recommendation: Audit the minimum OS and device requirements for the current release, and check whether the in-app update prompt blocks users who cannot upgrade. Where a device is unsupported, make the app fall back to the last compatible version instead of showing a forced-update screen, and test that re-login persists after a version update on both iOS and Android.

themes.label: Job description 'more' button broken
themes.summary: Many users report that the 'more' or 'read more' control on job descriptions does nothing, so they cannot read full requirements before applying, and it sometimes works only after closing and reopening the app. Reports are concentrated on Android in recent v4.1.12xx builds, and several say reinstalling or clearing cache did not help.
themes.recommendation: Reproduce the 'more' expansion failure on Android v4.1.1223 through v4.1.1245 across multiple devices, capture logs for the collapsed job description component, and ship a hotfix with a regression test covering expand and collapse on the job details screen.

themes.label: Unexpected charges and refund denials
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say they were auto-charged after a free trial or cancelled subscription, often without a clear reminder, and then had refund requests denied or left unanswered. Many point to a narrow refund window, refunds blocked by a single premium feature view, and support that offers only generic replies, with some also routed to Google Play or Apple for refunds. Several describe cancelled subscriptions still being billed or cut off early, and some report charges they never authorized.
themes.recommendation: Audit the free-trial-to-paid conversion flow and cancellation path end to end, including renewal reminder emails, the refund eligibility rule that treats viewing a profile as premium usage, and whether cancellations and in-app retention discounts are applied correctly across Google Play and App Store billing, then add a support escalation for refund cases that have been open more than a set number of days.

themes.label: AI-generated feed spam
themes.summary: Users say their feeds are now dominated by generic, AI-written posts (including AI slop and plagiarized content) that have replaced useful industry discussion. Many report that the "see fewer posts like this" and reporting options do nothing, and some link the decline to the platform pushing engagement-driven or short-form content. The complaints appear across both iOS and Android and across recent app versions.
themes.recommendation: Audit the feed ranking and moderation pipeline for AI-generated and plagiarized posts, and test whether the "I've seen too many posts about this topic" and "Show less like this" signals actually change ranking for a sample of affected users, fixing any signal that is logged but not applied.

themes.label: Praise for networking and job discovery
themes.summary: Most reviews in this cluster praise LinkedIn for professional networking, reconnecting with contacts, and finding opportunities, with many describing it as easy to use and a go-to career tool. Lower-rated reviews in the mix are more mixed, citing poor job search relevance, slow performance, messaging bugs, and frustration with premium pricing and unreturned job applications.
themes.recommendation: Protect the core networking and feed experience in roadmap decisions, and separately investigate the job search relevance and application-outcome complaints by reviewing recommended-job ranking and whether applications on Android and iOS are being delivered to recruiters correctly.

themes.label: Praise: professional networking value
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are overwhelmingly praising LinkedIn as a useful platform for professional networking, job searching, and career development, often calling it easy to use and a must-have tool. Several reviewers specifically value the professional tone compared with other social apps, and a few mention trust from verified profiles and the quality of industry content. No bugs or feature complaints stand out, though one reviewer asks for more business networking and recruitment features.
themes.recommendation: Protect the core networking and job-search flows in the next release, and run a short follow-up survey with users who mention business development or recruiting to scope the requested features for those audiences.

themes.label: iOS 16+ requirement blocks older devices
themes.summary: Many French-speaking iPhone and iPad users report being locked out after the update, with some saying the app stops loading or loops during update on older devices like a 4-year-old iPad or an iPhone 7 that cannot run iOS 18. Others mention login failures, including repeated six-digit code prompts and sync errors, and a few note the app now requires a newer iOS version. The cluster also includes unrelated praise and complaints about job recommendations, so the core theme is the loss of access on devices below the required OS.
themes.recommendation: Pull crash and update-failure logs for iOS 16 and 17 devices on app version 9.1.411 and later, confirm the minimum OS requirement, and either restore support for older iOS versions or show an in-app message with a clear fallback before the update is installed.

reviews.t: A professional platform with an embarrassingly unprofessional support system
reviews.x: LinkedIn restricted my account, required me to verify my identity using my passport through Persona, accepted the verification and still kept my account restricted without clearly explaining what I supposedly did wrong. The worst part is the support system. Trying to contact support simply sends me back to the login or identity-verification process I already completed. It is an absurd loop: verify, get rejected, ask for help, get sent back to verification. For a company that presents itself as the world’s leading professional networking platform, this is shockingly poor. If you restrict someone’s account after asking for sensitive identity documents, the bare minimum should be a clear reason, a transparent review process and access to a real human being. What is especially alarming is seeing multiple users recently reporting the exact same pattern: sudden restrictions, completed identity verification, rejected appeals and no real access to human support. At that point, this does not look like an isolated mistake it looks like a serious systemic failure. For a platform handling professional identities and sensitive documents, that is completely unacceptable Automated restrictions, automated responses, and practically inaccessible human support is not a serious security system. It is a broken process. Deeply disappointing and far below the standard expected from LinkedIn.

I remain an active and committed user of LinkedIn. It’s helped me build relationships, recruit great people, and win business. I believe in its potential. But lately, it feels like the platform is drifting from what made it valuable: helping real people connect around real opportunities. Today: • InMails have become noise - ignored and ineffective. • LinkedIn Ads are expensive, poorly targeted, and often under-deliver. • And the overall experience seems more optimized for monetizing attention than for enabling meaningful, high-value connections.
